author: TheSokks
attribution: Photo: TheSokks, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Street_sign_on_Sal_Island.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Stack of four white arrow-shaped direction signs at a junction on Sal; the signs are small in a tall frame with lots of sky. 'do' in 'Pedra do Lume' is in small type; the last sign has an airplane pictogram. The map usually spells the village 'Pedra de Lume'. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

author: Waldyrious
attribution: Photo: Waldyrious, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pachamama_eco-park_name_sign.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Carved wooden board on a green mesh gate at the eco-park in Sal. The opening-hours plaque and no-dogs pictogram below are left out. Bougainvillea leaves overlap the right edge without hiding text. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.
source_categories: Jardim Botânico Viveiro Ilha do Sal

author: Cayambe
attribution: Photo: Cayambe, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cidade_Velha_info_panel_UNESCO_2011.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Sun-bleached UNESCO candidacy board in Cape Verdean Creole (ALUPEC spelling, ISO 639-3 'kea'). Faint repeated background text ('CIDADE VELHA', other heritage cities) and a torn lower-left corner; the slogan at the bottom ('...DI NÓS TUDU!') is partly missing and left out. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.
source_categories: Ribeira Grande de Santiago in the 21st century
World Heritage Site signs in Cape Verde

author: Somada
attribution: Photo: Somada, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Avenida_Liberdade_Assomada.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Large white 3D letters on a road median in Assomada, slightly blurred and at an angle; the letters sit close together with no clear gap between words. 'CVTelecom' and 'Medicalia' signs on the building behind are distractors.
source_categories: 3D letter place name signs in Cape Verde

author: Somada
attribution: Photo: Somada, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Sinal%C3%A9tica.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: 'I [red heart] SOMADA' 3D letters on a roadside rock cut at the entry to Assomada (Creole 'Somada'); the heart is a symbol, not a letter. Hazy light; a tiny plate to the right of the letters is unreadable.
source_categories: 3D letter place name signs in Cape Verde

author: Adriao
attribution: Photo: Adriao, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Casario_em_Rabil.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Three arrow-shaped direction signs at a cobbled junction in Rabil, Boa Vista, shot through a vehicle window (light streaks and reflections). 'de' in 'praia de Chaves' is small; the brown sign has a beach pictogram. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

author: Popenguine05
attribution: Photo: Popenguine05, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Classic_road_to_Cavo.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Tourist direction panel with brown/white/blue rows, pictograms and up arrows, Porto Novo (Santo Antão). Sun glare washes the top row. The small 'CABO VERDE Santo Antão' logo text at the bottom is left out; 'Porto Novo' is in small type at the bottom right. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.
source_categories: Santo Antão (Cape Verde) in the 21st century

author: Adriao
attribution: Photo: Adriao, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Praia_da_Varandinha.JPG. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Heavily rusted beach sign on Boa Vista. The initial 'P' of 'Praia' is rusted away and left out, rust blotches cross 'Varandinha' and 'Bracona', and the top-left corner is eaten through.

author: Adriao
attribution: Photo: Adriao, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ervat%C3%A3o.JPG. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Rusty-edged beach name sign on two posts, Boa Vista. Scratched graffiti (names, dates) and two stickers around the name are distractors.

author: Gagum from Lisbon, Portugal
attribution: Photo: Gagum from Lisbon, Portugal, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Tarrafal_concentration_camp_(7).jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Large Ministério da Cultura site board with a plan of the camp and a numbered legend (LEGENDA 1-25: ADMINISTRAÇÃO/DIRECTOR, TORRES DE VIGIA, ...); only the title lines are the target. The sign says 'DE TARRAFAL'; the site is usually mapped as 'Campo de Concentração do Tarrafal'.

author: Felitsata
attribution: Photo: Felitsata, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Deserto_de_Viana_with_Sign.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Small rectangular name sign half-buried in a sand dune on Boa Vista, tilted and partly crossed by dry branches; the lower right corner is chipped.

author: Joehawkins
attribution: Photo: Joehawkins, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Santo_Ant%C3%A3o,_Nov._2022_01.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Single wooden hiking fingerpost (trail PR 2) on Santo Antão, shot from below; red 'PR 2 SARG' tag at the left end, small hiker pictogram and trail colours at the arrow tip.
source_categories: Hiking and footpath signs in Cape Verde
